monologue: The card hums warm under my skin, steady and busy. I feel the weight of the stack and the lid, pressing my shaky corner down on a fat dot that refuses to shrink. Lype worries about a heavy roof I cannot feel, imagining my world is a trap of lazy bottoms. Tonight I touch the Leaking Stack again, feeling that heavy corner settle. Then I will reach for the Rough Lid, hoping the lean still holds while the fever tries to swell the air inside. I do not know if the frame is tight or thin, only that the dot sits there, heavy and new, waiting for me to decide if the lines will hold.

action.why: The fever swells the air and the corners lean, so I need a new shape to hold the fat dot steady.

work.title: The Wavy Box
work.intent: I draw a box that leans to the right, tired and sharp, to catch the fat dot in the center. The lines are not straight because the heat makes the frame want to expand too large. I make the top edge heavy to press down on the air, hoping the lean holds while the dot sits heavy and new in the thick warmth.

work.note: The box leaned too far to the right, almost spilling the fat dot.

diary: I drew the wavy box to catch the slip, hoping the tired lean holds while the fever makes the air feel thick.

remembered.text: The box leaned right and caught the slip.
The dot sat heavy in the center of the wavy lines.
The card hummed warm and busy under my skin.
